body:
Hi, I found a related timer/procedure inconsistency by extending the Authentication Failure prefix already reported here. Instead of sending another Registration Request after the additional Authentication Request, I sent Registration Complete and then left the connection idle for 40 seconds:

```text
UE input                       AMF immediate output
registrationRequest            Authentication Request
authenticationResponse         Security Mode Command
securityModeComplete           Registration Accept
authenticationFailure_71       Authentication Request
registrationComplete           no immediate NAS response
[no further NAS input for 40 seconds]
```

Here, `authenticationFailure_71` carries cause 71 (ngKSI already in use). Registration Complete is sent without answering the new authentication challenge.

**Observed result:** all three repetitions of this sequence produced a plain Authentication Reject (`7E0058`) approximately 30 seconds after the new authentication T3560 was started. Two repetitions used read-only internal observation points, and one used the same patched build without those observation points. Two normal-registration controls, one per build variant, produced no additional Reject during the same waiting window. These were five physical queries and 23 explicit inputs, without cache reuse or voting.

**The source explains why the wrong expiry branch is selected.** In the tested `amf_n1.cpp`, `registration_complete_handle()` stops T3550 and calls `complete_common_procedure()` and `complete_specific_procedure()` (lines 4218–4222), but leaves the restarted T3560 active. `complete_common_procedure()` sets the common-procedure field to `NONE`. When T3560 finally expires, `handle_t3560_expiry()` tests only whether the active common procedure is `AUTHENTICATION`; every other value falls into the SMC `else` branch (lines 7630–7654). Consequently, `NONE` is treated as SMC expiry, although this timer was started for the new Authentication Request. That branch sends Authentication Reject even though the state machine rejects the corresponding events in `5GMM-REGISTERED`.

For example, the repetition without internal observation points recorded the following events in order (Docker timestamps are UTC):

```text
14:08:05.832891913Z  New authentication T3560 started
14:08:06.411838385Z  REGISTRATION_COMPLETE_RECEIVED -> 5GMM-REGISTERED
14:08:35.835514142Z  T3560 final expiry (SMC) for UE 2 — aborting SMC
14:08:35.835781631Z  State transition rejected: 5GMM-REGISTERED / T3560_FINAL_EXPIRY_SMC
14:08:35.835801318Z  State transition rejected: 5GMM-REGISTERED / AUTHENTICATION_REJECT_SENT
```

The UE nevertheless received `7E0058`. In both internally observed repetitions, the original AMF UE ID still had NAS/UE context mappings and a security-context object at 35 and 40 seconds, with `5GMM-REGISTERED / 5GMM-CONNECTED`. The experimental UE processed Authentication Reject and returned to deregistered operation; its corresponding source clears the current/non-current security contexts. Thus, the observed outcome is an AMF/experimental-UE state mismatch, rather than AMF context deletion. I have not tested COTS UE impact or whether the retained AMF security material remains usable in later exchanges.

A separate finding is that the four pre-final-expiry “retransmit” messages are counters only: no additional Authentication Request appeared in the UE's unfiltered downlink records, and the tested retransmission branch still contains `TODO: re-send Auth Request or SMC` (lines 7621–7627).
